answered.sql: SELECT system_name FROM Systems WHERE system_id IN (SELECT system_id FROM It_Support_Specialists_Systems GROUP BY system_id HAVING COUNT(it_specialist_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM It_Support_Specialists))

candidates.meaning: Return a list of systems that each support specialist works with, ensuring no specialist is listed more than once per system.
candidates.sql: SELECT DISTINCT s.system_name, i.name FROM It_Support_Specialists i JOIN It_Support_Specialists_Systems iss ON i.id = iss.it_specialist_id JOIN Systems s ON iss.system_id = s.system_id

candidates.meaning: List all systems that each support specialist works with.
candidates.sql: SELECT s.name AS specialist_name, GROUP_CONCAT(sys.system_name) AS systems_worked_with FROM It_Support_Specialists s JOIN It_Support_Specialists_Systems iss ON s.id = iss.it_specialist_id JOIN Systems sys ON iss.system_id = sys.system_id GROUP BY s.id

candidates.meaning: Identify the systems each support specialist is associated with, including specialists who might not be assigned to any system.
candidates.sql: SELECT s.name AS specialist_name, GROUP_CONCAT(sys.system_name) AS systems_worked_with FROM It_Support_Specialists s LEFT JOIN It_Support_Specialists_Systems iss ON s.id = iss.it_specialist_id LEFT JOIN Systems sys ON iss.system_id = sys.system_id GROUP BY s.id
